correctness.rationale: The argument is valid for finite nonzero associative unital rings with independent uniformly sampled factors and every integer k>=1. Nilpotence descends and lifts through the finite nilpotent Jacobson radical. The Fitting direct-sum count establishes exactly q^{r(r-1)} nilpotent matrices in M_r(F_q). Given the first k-1 factors C of rank r, the product CA_k restricted to im(C) is uniformly distributed on End(im(C)), so its chance of nilpotence is q^{-r}; this equals the chance a uniform vector lies in ker(C). Starting from a nonzero vector, each independent uniform matrix returns zero with chance q^{-n}, proving 1-(1-q^{-n})^k in each simple matrix factor. Direct product independence gives the stated product formula; extracting the largest exponential rate and its multiplicity iteratively from 1-P_k proves the multiset-of-q_i^{n_i} converse. The k=1 identity and all boundary cases n_i=1 are covered. Fresh exact enumeration M_2(F_2), k=1,2,3 confirmed probabilities 1/4, 7/16, 37/64, which corroborate but do not establish the general proof.
